summary: Completed a real paid Ausca media.transcription run for Frantic #133, including immutable artifact commit, live x402 challenge, Base USDC settlement, asynchronous invocation polling, digest validation, and public receipt verification; the run also exposed concrete replay, response-shape, receipt-verification, and transcription-quality issues.

successful_invocation.transcript: Frantic Bounty 133 media transcription verification. This short recording tests the OSCA transcription workflow from artifact commit through receipt validation.

segments.text: This short recording tests the OSCA transcription workflow from artifact commit through receipt validation.

receipt.note: Runx public page is hash-only L1 notarization and explicitly does not independently prove the blockchain transaction; Base USDC transfer was verified separately.

observations.detail: Committed a 488,328-byte WAV as an immutable Ausca artifact; returned artifact content_digest exactly matched the local SHA-256.
Read live media.transcription offer revision transcription-bytes-r6 and pinned revision/input/output schema digests before invoking.
Unsigned POST returned x402 v2 PAYMENT-REQUIRED for exactly 400000 atomic USDC on eip155:8453, payTo 0x26572ff23c6c52bfb1a69cb0c9114a8be443b422.

An earlier invocation identity returned HTTP 200 with status=refused, code=replay_conflict after a fresh payment authorization was attempted against the reused idempotency identity; no PAYMENT-RESPONSE was present and no outgoing USDC transfer was found for that attempt.
Generated a new invocation/idempotency identity while retaining the same immutable audio artifact; fresh invocation was paid_5ea32dea-c072-440e-abeb-4c7fb25b3212.
EIP-3009/x402 authorization settled 0.40 USDC on Base in tx 0xfefe9486fb16633d7ed52a880c189ee58d2509f5f0627090b30eafdd747eaae2 at 2026-09-22T01:50:15Z.
Invocation remained asynchronous after admission and reached state=succeeded at 2026-09-22T01:50:57.040Z.
Output source_digest exactly matched the committed artifact digest; output_digest was sha256:303767a3038ff710f8283e037ddf971a8557c872d37c02cdc68e0f24c1bf6274; two timed segments were returned.
The spoken proper name 'Ausca' in the second sentence was transcribed as 'OSCA', a concrete proper-noun recognition error in an otherwise accurate short clip.
Terminal invocation exposed Runx receipt 0dffa555...e69a1; public page says Published by Ausca, Media Transcription completed, declared amount 0.40 USD.

Fresh successful invocation path from prepared challenge at 01:48:52.266Z to receipt notarization at 01:51:11.041Z took about 138.8s. Including the earlier replay-conflict debugging from initial artifact creation at 01:28:50.875Z took about 22m20s.

issues.detail: POST /v1/transcribe-media may return HTTP 200 for a semantic refusal. A client that treats 200 as success without parsing body.status can hide actionable codes such as replay_conflict.

Reusing an invocation/idempotency identity with a newly generated payment authorization produced replay_conflict. The safe recovery path was not obvious until canonical invocation and chain state were separately reconciled, then a fresh idempotency identity was created.

The public Runx receipt intentionally omits wallet addresses and transaction identifiers, so validating the actual Base USDC transfer required a separate chain read even though the page declared 0.40 USD.
The transcription changed the spoken product name 'Ausca' to 'OSCA' in the second sentence.

proposed_change: Add a short paid-invocation decision table to the Media Transcription SKILL: parse body.status even on HTTP 200; for status=refused surface code/reason verbatim; for replay_conflict instruct callers to reconcile GET /v1/invocations/{id} plus settlement state before deciding whether a fresh idempotency identity is safe. This would have prevented two opaque payment attempts and made recovery deterministic.
